description: The figure illustrates five schematic bar-chart patterns for distributing layers across four groups (G₁ to G₄), with each mini-chart labeled below as Increasing, Uniform, Decreasing, Spindle, and Bottleneck. In each mini-chart, the horizontal axis contains the group categories arranged left to right from G₁ through G₄ (no explicit tick labels are shown), and the vertical axis represents the number of layers per group on a linear scale spanning approximately 1 to 5 layers (no numeric tick marks are displayed). All bars are rendered in a pale green fill with thin dark outlines and no legend. In the Increasing pattern, four bars rise from left to right with approximate heights 1 (G₁), 2 (G₂), 4 (G₃), and 5 (G₄). In the Uniform pattern, all four bars are equal at about 3 layers each. In the Decreasing pattern, the bars descend left to right at approximately 5 (G₁), 4 (G₂), 3 (G₃), and 1 (G₄). In the Spindle pattern, the outer bars are shorter and the middle bars are taller, with approximate heights 1 (G₁), 4 (G₂), 4 (G₃), and 1 (G₄). In the Bottleneck pattern, the outer bars are taller than the middle bars, with approximate heights 4 (G₁), 2 (G₂), 2 (G₃), and 4 (G₄). The bars within each mini-chart are not presented as globally sorted beyond the pattern-specific ordering implied by the labels, and no bars are specially emphasized with annotations or distinct styling.
caption_used: The bar chart depicts five distinct layer distribution patterns across groups (G_1 to G_4), labeled as 'Increasing,' 'Uniform,' 'Decreasing,' 'Spindle,' and 'Bottleneck.' The horizontal axis represents the group categories, while the vertical axis indicates the approximate number of layers per group, with values ranging from 1 to 5. In the 'Increasing' pattern, the bars rise progressively from left to right, starting at 1 and peaking at 5. The 'Uniform' distribution maintains a consistent height of 3 layers across all groups. The 'Decreasing' pattern demonstrates a sharp decline, beginning at 5 layers and reducing to 1. The 'Spindle' distribution exhibits a symmetrical rise and fall, with the central group reaching 4 layers, flanked by groups of 2 layers each. Notably, the 'Bottleneck' distribution stabilizes at 2 layers in the middle groups, while the outer groups each contain 4 layers, creating a pronounced dip. Comparatively, the 'Spindle' pattern consistently exceeds the 'Bottleneck' in central group height, and the rate of increase in the 'Increasing' pattern is roughly linear, with no abrupt transitions.
